author: Inside Edition
description: A man made himself at home at a house that was not his. The man drank a bottle of alcohol and fell asleep on the couch during an open house in Florida, the homeowner says. Stephanie says the man wrote her a letter of apology taking full accountability. Open house tours are a popular way of selling your home, but they can come with risks. Inside Edition shares tips on how to help protect your belongings when you're holding an open house.
title: Tips To Protect Your Belongings During Open House

author: Inside Edition
description: Two sisters took their very first ride in a driverless Waymo when the car tried to get across a four lane of a highway so it could make a left into another four lanes of traffic. Then, it stopped in the path of oncoming traffic. The sisters spoke with Inside Edition. Waymo tells Inside Edition "while the event does not reflect the vast majority of our services, we take it seriously to learn and improve from it."
title: Sisters Terrified After Their Driverless Waymo Nearly Caused Crash

author: Inside Edition
description: The Oscars red carpet has been rolled out in preparation for Sunday's ceremony. This year, the Academy Awards take place in the shadow of the war in Iran and fears of a terrorist attack in the United States. The Oscars will have more security and police. US authorities have reportedly picked up an eerie series of coded short wave radio messages broadcast from Tehran. The Department of Homeland Security is warning that the coded messages may activate Iranian-backed sleeper cells in the US.
title: Heightened Security At This Year's Oscars Amid War In Iran

author: Inside Edition
description: In a brazen heist that is becoming more common, two men stole gas from U-Haul trucks. They drilled into the gas tanks when the gas caught fire and trucks became engulfed in a giant ball of flame. Haydn Hall, the general manager of the U-Haul depot near Seattle spoke with Inside Edition about the heists. The price of gas is surging because of the conflict with Iran. There is no relief in sight as Iran was vowed to disrupt the flow of oil.
title: Brazen Thieves Steal Gas From U-Haul Trucks

author: Inside Edition
description: The student charged with homicide after a graduation prank went wrong is breaking his silence. Authorities say Jason Hughes died after he slipped and fell in front of a car. The vehicle was allegedly being driven by 18-year-old Jayden Wallace. Before it turned tragic, the plan to toilet paper the teacher's house was described as "a good-natured prank." Wallace now says "I pledge to live out the remainder of my life in a manner that honors the memory of Coach Hughes." Hughes' wife has requested that the charges be dismissed.
title: Student Charged With Homicide Of Prank Gone Wrong Speaks Out

author: Inside Edition
description: In 2017, Professor Robert Kelly's then 4-year-old daughter hopped into his home office and crashed her dad's live TV interview in a moment that blew up the internet. The political science professor did his best to shoo her away and kept on talking. Then his 9-month-old son waddles into the room in a walker. Kelly's wife slid in to round up the kids and turned the interview to chaos. The family spoke with Inside Edition nine years later.
title: Where Is The Family At Center Of Viral Live TV Interview Now?

author: Inside Edition
description: A former pro-football player is charged with killing his girlfriend, and prosecutors reportedly said he used ChatGPT to try to help him cover it up. Darron Lee, 31, appeared in a Tennessee court to face charges of first degree murder and tampering with and/or fabricating evidence, according to online court records. The Hamilton County Sheriff says Lee's girlfriend, Gabriella Perpetuo, 29, was found dead in a home in Ooltewah on February 5.  Inside Edition Digital’s Mara Montalbano has more.
title: Ex-NFLer Accused Of Using ChatGPT To Help With Answer About Girlfriend's Death

author: Inside Edition
description: In a growing trend called teen takeovers, large groups of rowdy kids are organizing mass meetups on social media at shopping malls and other public spaces. The chaotic events sometimes result in fights, theft, and wanton destruction. Now, police are cracking down on the unruly teenagers, using state-of-the-art surveillance technology to try to stop the takeovers before they get out of hand.
title: Cops Use Cameras and Drones to Crack Down on Takeovers

author: Inside Edition
description:
Millennials and Gen Zers are now embracing the 200-year-old game Mahjong. Meghan Markle hosts a mahjong game night with friends as seen on her Netflix Show. Leland restaurant in Brooklyn hosts mahjong classes. "It's really about learning the game and being able to play amongst a bunch of friends and new friends," Leland owner Randi Lee tells Inside Edition. Mahjong instructor Lenny An, spoke with Inside Edition about how the game can bring people together.

More information about Leland Brooklyn: https://www.lelandbrooklyn.com/
title: Young Adults Are Embracing The 200-Year-Old Game Mahjong
